title: DbContext service lifetimes configuration and providers
concepts: DbContext is an EF Core unit of work: it tracks changes, builds queries, coordinates provider services, and persists updates. It is short-lived and not thread-safe.

Dependency injection commonly registers one context per request scope. Factories are useful when a longer-lived service must create separate units of work; pooling reuses instances and requires careful state-reset boundaries.

A provider translates EF operations to a database-specific query and update surface. Provider packages and EF Core versions must be compatible; LINQ portability is not complete abstraction of database differences.
Configuration options include logging, warnings, tracking defaults, connection behavior, and design-time construction. Sensitive-data logging can expose secrets and should be restricted.
Schema creation, migrations, and database initialization are different operations; EnsureCreated is not a substitute for a migration-managed schema.
